source.text: Calendarul zilei, Doxologia (doxologia.ro), 10 decembrie — «Sfântul Mucenic Ermoghen»
saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 10ης Δεκεμβρίου — «Άγιοι Μηνάς ο Καλλικέλαδος, Ερμογένης και Εύγραφος»

attestations.note: The life page heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 10 Δεκεμβρίου εκάστου έτους», the same day the folder already keeps, and the entry is the same man: the Athenian scholar sent as eparch to replace Menas, who tortured him, found his wounds healed, and became a Christian at his answer. saint.gr does not call him a bishop, so the folder's existing `bishop` type is left alone and nothing is added to it from this page. **The page will not settle the reign** — Maximinus, 311 to 313, or, it allows, Maximian, 286 to 305 — so no `dates` object is proposed. Of the page's four hymns only the first apolytikion, «Δι' ἐγκρατείας», speaks of the three martyrs in the plural and is their common; it is copied here. The other apolytikion and the kontakion address Menas by name and are taken in his folder only, and the kathisma, which names all three, is not a kind the schema holds. No asterisk and no «Δεν είναι διασταυρωμένη» sentence.
Not checked: the Ohrid Prologue as printed by pravoslavno.rs (25 September 2026).

hymns.text: Cu înfrânarea omorând pornirile și îndemnurile cele arzătoare ale patimilor, ucenicii lui Hristos au luat harul de a alunga urmările bolilor celor neputincioși și a face minuni, atât în viață, cât și după moarte. Minune uimitoare cu adevărat! Că oase goale izvorăsc tămăduiri. Slavă Ție, Singurului Dumnezeu și Ziditorului.

source.text: Doxologia — Troparul Sfinților Mucenici Mina, Ermoghen și Evgraf (one hymn printed for the three together; the page prints no glas)

english.text: Having put to death by abstinence the burning stirrings and promptings of the passions, the disciples of Christ received the grace to drive away the effects of the sicknesses of the infirm and to work wonders, both in life and after death. A marvel indeed: that bare bones pour out healings. Glory to you, the only God and Maker.

hymns.text: Δι' ἐγκρατείας, τῶν παθῶν τὰς πυριφλέκτους, ἀπονεκρώσαντες ὁρμὰς καὶ τὰς κινήσεις, τοῦ Χριστοῦ οἱ Μάρτυρες ἔλαβον τὴν χάριν, τὰς νόσους ἀποδιώκειν τῶν ἀσθενῶν, καὶ ζῶντες καὶ μετὰ τέλος θαυματουργεῖν· ὄντως θαῦμα παράδοξον! ὅτι ὀστέα γυμνά, ἐκβλύζουσιν ἰάματα. Δόξα τῷ μόνῳ Θεῷ ἡμῶν.

source.text: saint.gr, Ἀπολυτίκιον, Ἦχος πλ. δ’, Τὸ προσταχθὲν — the first hymn on the page of «Άγιοι Μηνάς ο Καλλικέλαδος, Ερμογένης και Εύγραφος»; it is the common of the three martyrs, in the plural, printed as their service.

english.text: Having put to death by abstinence the fire-burning rushes and motions of the passions, the martyrs of Christ received the grace to drive away the diseases of the sick and to work wonders both while they lived and after their end. Truly a strange wonder, that bare bones should pour out healings! Glory to our only God.
